I a way, yes. The "Crisis" storyline, at first, was decided because there were too many alternate earths and times - the story's universe was getting out of hand, it was better to write an end to it and "restart" with something cleaner. Some characters had 3 or 4 alternate origin stories…

Of course it did not take long before things got all chaotic again, but it's expectable, with so many writers and artists with their own ideas.

I tend to see the Sotm->OblivAeon->Tactics evolution this way.  The event gives a good reason to stop having to think about alternate timelines and universe, and go into new directions.

If it was a real comics series, I would say that a new manager decided to "modernize" the comics with the help of new writers. More modern look for the heroes, some changes in the role of characters, new themes, new menaces, new look and feel… And also a good way to make everyone "a little older" and bring a new generation of heroes.

Rabit:

 

TheSoundOfTrees wrote:
The "Crisis" storyline, at first, was decided because there were too many alternate earths and times - the story's universe was getting out of hand, it was better to write an end to it and "restart" with something cleaner. Some characters had 3 or 4 alternate origin stories...

Of course. But I think the Event, like the whole game, is an hommage to this kind of things happening in "real" comic books. Crisis, Civil War, House of M, all these "big" events that "change" at least temporarily the way the universe of the comic book line works.

Of course, in the "real world" these events have many reasons : the whim of an author or lead, the necessity to clean the line, a fall in sales leading to desperate measures or in "writing out" heroes that don't sell much, etc. GtG do this on purpose, and with a lot of preparation - but they do it because it happens in comic books.

In the end, the status quo won't change much : a handful of characters lost or changed mainly. The big big change is the loss of "alternate" timelines and universe, the limitation on planar travel, and the importance of Oblivion Shards. I am very curious to see what kind of story lines we will have in future products…

Akash'Bhuta is a perfect example of what I mean.  First there's Akash'Bhuta, and then Akash'Thriya working with the heroes, and then Akash'Darsha, who is villainous again, but different from before.

 

In her case she literally is a different type of being.

 

Akash'Bhuta is the manifestation of the earth after amassing X energy over the course of centuries. She then fights the Argent Adept and generally is defeated and the cycle begins anew.

 

Akash'Thriya is a desperate re-manisfestation in response to OblivAeon, she was only defeated a short while ago, she doesn't have enough strength to fully remanisfest. In addition, her goal is protection instead of devastation and recreation, which is a complete different goal than the spirit of Akash' generally has. Also Akash'Thriya is defeated and then takes power from the Void, changing her further.

 

This taking of power from the Void and a run in with the Oblivion Shards is what creates Akash'Darsha. She realized she can gather power more quickly through these methods than her normal methods and the shards have begun changing her. For example, while she has a giant manisfestation as Akash'Darsha, she also has Avatars more similiar to Akash'Thriya which she can send out to act seperately from herself. She is not the same being she was, she is more active, more violent, less stable, and her goals may be more gathering power than destruction and recreation, as she has realized the allure of power and what it can do for her.

posts.cooked:
torian:

The whole Blade/Luminary thing reminds me a lot of when Baron Zemo changed his name to Citizen V when Thunderbolts launched.

That's just it, though: the whole premise of Thunderbolts was that it was (spoilers for a comic which, whilst 20 years old, is still my favorite team book of all time) the Masters of Evil fooling the world into believing they were new superheroes.  They had new names because nobody knew it was them.  And, of course, most of them end up becoming the heroes they pretended to be and keeping those names (though Zemo not so much).  The names are, in other words, an integral statement about their character arcs.

 

Luminary isn't like that.  From what Christopher has said, it sounds like he's not even pretending.  It's not Zemo in Thunderbolts, it's Luthor in Destroyer.  But… Luthor didn't start going by Man Of Scalp or whatever for his five-minute team-up with Superman.  He went by Lex Luthor.

 

I really should opt out of this argument, because it's such a small thing and we've all heard each other at great length already, but at this point, my obsession with details works against me.  This is something which is at odds with the genre conventions.  That's not bad in and of itself, lots of good things come from disregarding convention, but I just squirm a little when people act like it's not a little unusual.  Knowing what something is remains valid, regerdless on your feelsings for it, specifically.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
I think that I'm going to imagine it like this:

 

News People:  "So, we hear that a big evil space guy is trying to destroy the world."

Legacy: "Yes, OblivAeon is quite dangerous.  We've pulled out all the stops to protect the world.  We've even teamed up with Baron Blade."

News People: "WHAT! Baron Blade!  But he's evil!  He tried to crash the moon into the Earth!  And then tried to blow up Megalopolis!  We can't say that you're teaming up with Baron Blade!"

Legacy: "But we are.  And not just him.  Among the alternate universe heroes that we've summoned there's an alternate version of Ivan, who calls herself Luminary and is a hero like we are.  She's joining us too."

News People: "Luminary.  That's not a bad name.  Okay, we'll say that you're teaming up with Luminary and alternate Luminary.  That'll work."

 

That narrative makes sense to me - It's not that Baron Blade starts going by Luminary, but he coopts the name from the real Luminary when she joins us from another world as a PR stunt.  And then once OblivAeon is over, he goes back to his old path and name.


For Ambuscade, this explaination doesn't work as well, because he had abandoned his villainy and returned to stunt work before the OblivAeon events.  In his case, I'd say that OblivAeon reawoke his desire for big game hunting and pulled him out of retirment, but he switched from hero hunting to mercenary work (which involves some hero hunting.  But also villain hunting).  But while he might have benefited from cleaning his slate and starting over with a new name, as a mercenary he benefitted more from his previous credentials and reputation, so he went back to using the name Ambuscade.

 

In both cases, though, I'd consider the "alternate world" versions to be the "true" version, and the villains-turned-hero to be the variants.  So I'm hoping that they show up frequently in the art and flavor text.

posts.name: phantaskippy

It will be interesting to see how they rule the Void guard.

Because as of right now, everything in the game that refers to a card name or keyword will search the entire table for that name or keyword.

That's why If Pride or Prejudice is borrowed by Guise and the other is in Expat's area when Pride is used you can use Prejudice and you end up with both Guise and Expat dealing 2 projectile damage.

Its why Omnitron-X's Self Sabotage can be used to destroy Omnitron's components, and the unofficial ruling on multiple decks with the same name goes along with it.

Before Christopher stated that they would have the same names and rules would be added 100% of this game fell directly in line with my statements.

 

It is not a logical fallacy to use all the information you have at hand to analyze a new set of information.

It is logically flawed to accuse someone of a logical fallacy because in the future they were proven wrong.

Also, we have to apply the rules we have to the situations that apply in the game the best we can.  Otherwise it is all house rules.  Every single rule in this game carries with it a caveat of "unless otherwise stated", if you look at my posting record you will see me bring that up a lot.

I was wrong, but there was nothing wrong with the process that led me there, the rules are going to change, but as of right now you can't have 2 targets with the same name in a game without making house rules.  Expecting that to change is less logical than expecting it to stay the same.
